contact:
Corrections are welcome, and they are the most useful thing a reader can send. If an entry misstates a claim, a ruling or a source, say which entry, what it says, and what the source says instead. A correction that cites the source is checked against it.

Suggestions for questions the site has not yet answered are welcome too. Put the question the way you would put it to a friend.

If you are writing because you are in crisis, do not wait for a reply. Talk to someone today, and find a helpline near you.
privacy:
This page describes what the site stores and sends, and what it does not.

Reading the site

The theme loads no analytics, advertising or tracking scripts. Reading times are worked out on the server from the text of the page, and nothing about your visit is sent anywhere to do it.

The typefaces are served from this site. Your browser does not contact a font service to display a page.

The images shown when a page is shared are generated on this site from the page's own text.

Sharing

The share buttons are plain links. Nothing loads from WhatsApp, Telegram or any other service until you choose one, and choosing one opens that service, which then handles what you send under its own terms. The copy-link button uses your own browser's clipboard. Nobody is told that you shared a page.

Searching

Searches run on this site. The theme sends your search to no other service, and search results are kept out of search engines.

Comments

Where comments are open, WordPress stores the name, email address and comment you submit, and by default your IP address and browser details, to help detect spam. Your email address is never shown. WordPress may display an avatar next to a comment, and its default avatars are fetched from Gravatar, an outside service, using a scrambled form of the email address.

Cookies

The theme sets no cookies. WordPress sets cookies for people who log in, and remembers a commenter's name and email in a cookie only when the commenter asks it to.
